abstracts.abstract: This paper proposes a novel theoretical framework for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assisted wireless communications, fundamentally shifting from conventional channel modeling approaches. Unlike existing paradigms that rely on deterministic or simplified statistical models, we develop a unified mathematical framework integrating stochastic geometry and random matrix theory to characterize the complex electromagnetic interactions between RIS elements and scattered propagation paths. The proposed framework introduces a three-dimensional spatial scattering model that captures the anisotropic reflection patterns and mutual coupling effects inherent in large-scale RIS deployments. Based on this framework, we derive closed-form expressions for key performance metrics including outage probability, ergodic capacity, and energy efficiency. Our analysis reveals fundamental scaling laws relating RIS surface area, element count, and communication reliability that were previously unknown. Numerical results demonstrate that the theoretical predictions align closely with full-wave electromagnetic simulations, validating the framework's accuracy. More importantly, this work establishes a paradigm shift by providing rigorous analytical tools for RIS-enabled communication system design, enabling systematic optimization that was previously infeasible. The proposed framework opens new research directions in intelligent reflecting surface theory and provides essential guidelines for practical RIS deployment in next-generation wireless networks.

This paper presents a significantly improved theoretical analysis of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems operating under imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC), addressing a critical gap in existing literature where perfect SIC is typically assumed. While prior works have established fundamental NOMA performance bounds under ideal conditions, practical implementations inevitably suffer from residual interference due to hardware impairments and channel estimation errors. We develop a comprehensive mathematical framework that accurately models the SIC error propagation phenomenon and its impact on system-level performance. Specifically, we derive novel closed-form expressions for the outage probability and sum rate of a two-user downlink NOMA system, incorporating realistic SIC residual error models that follow Gaussian distribution with variance proportional to signal power. The analytical results reveal that existing perfect SIC analyses overestimate system performance by up to 40% in practical scenarios with moderate error levels. Furthermore, we propose an optimized power allocation strategy that maximizes system throughput while satisfying individual user quality-of-service requirements under the new error model. Simulation results confirm the accuracy of our theoretical derivations and demonstrate that the proposed power allocation scheme achieves substantial performance improvements compared to conventional approaches designed for ideal conditions. This work provides valuable insights for practical NOMA system design and deployment.

This paper presents a novel deep learning-enabled UAV-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) system architecture that fundamentally transforms task offloading paradigms in beyond 5G networks. Unlike conventional MEC systems that rely on static edge servers and predefined offloading strategies, the proposed system employs a deep reinforcement learning framework to enable autonomous, real-time task scheduling decisions for aerial computing platforms. The system architecture integrates multiple functional modules: a convolutional neural network-based environment perception module, a long short-term memory network for wireless channel prediction, and a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) agent for joint computation resource allocation and trajectory planning. The UAV platform is equipped with a heterogeneous computing architecture comprising multi-core CPUs and GPU accelerators to handle diverse computational tasks efficiently. A critical innovation lies in the designed attention mechanism that dynamically adjusts offloading decisions based on real-time channel conditions, user mobility patterns, and computational workload characteristics. Implementation results on a software-defined radio testbed demonstrate that the proposed system achieves task completion latency below 15 milliseconds while maintaining energy consumption within specified limits. Compared to state-of-the-art schemes, the proposed design improves system energy efficiency by 42% and reduces average processing delay by 35%, establishing a new paradigm for intelligent edge computing in aerial networks.

This paper presents a significantly improved hybrid beamforming design for multi-user massive MIMO-OFDM systems in millimeter-wave communications, addressing the critical challenges of high hardware complexity and large channel estimation overhead in existing approaches. While conventional hybrid precoding architectures achieve near-optimal performance with fully connected structures, they require a large number of radio frequency chains, resulting in prohibitive hardware cost and power consumption. We propose a novel sparse hybrid precoding framework with dynamic subarray configuration that adaptively activates different subarrays based on instantaneous channel conditions. The proposed architecture employs a reduced number of phase shifters while maintaining beamforming gain through sophisticated angular domain processing. Specifically, we develop a two-stage hybrid precoding algorithm: first, a compressive sensing-based channel estimation scheme that exploits the sparse nature of millimeter-wave channels to reduce pilot overhead by 60%; second, an iterative optimization algorithm that jointly designs the analog and digital precoder matrices under hardware constraints. Implementation on a software-defined radio platform operating at 28 GHz demonstrates that the proposed design achieves spectral efficiency within 1.5 dB of fully digital precoding while reducing hardware complexity by 75%. The system supports adaptive modulation up to 64-QAM with aggregate throughput exceeding 10 Gbps, representing a substantial improvement over existing hybrid beamforming solutions for practical deployment.
